scripts: autoresearch/experiments/h4-dynamics/code/hand_synthetic_pose_check.py (new, addendum for Part 2's meal_seq131 pose question)

part1_which_variant.answer: Both #28 (hand_pixel_stats.py) and #31 (hands_pose_depth.py) build a SINGLE AriaDigitalTwinDataProvider from get_datapaths(skeleton_flag=True) and read segmentation AND depth from that same provider -- no seg/depth mismatch between the two streams in either script. The concern that they might differ does not apply here.
part1_which_variant.read: GT depth DOES see the person under skeleton_flag=True: at dynamic-segmentation pixels the with-skeleton depth is consistently near-camera (0.09-0.88 m median across the three sequences) while the without-skeleton depth at the SAME pixels is consistently the background behind them (0.71-2.38 m) -- essentially every dynamic pixel (>=99.5%) differs by more than 5cm between the two variants. Alignment between the segmentation mask and RGB/depth was independently verified at native 1408x1408 resolution (overlay, not resized) before trusting this.

part1_restated_28_numbers: #28's dyn-depth medians (reported as 0.26-0.94 m across the three sequences) are CONFIRMED under the correct (with-skeleton) variant -- this run's median_with_m values (0.306, 0.092, 0.881) bracket the same range on a fresh 20-frame high-dyn_frac sample. Nothing to correct or withdraw.

part2_synthetic_hands_free.read: 2/3 sequences show a clear gap (dynamic pixels differ from synthetic far more than static ones: 0.180 vs 0.111 golden_seq100; 0.216 vs 0.101 party_seq101) consistent with the person being absent from the synthetic render. meal_seq131 is the outlier (0.254 vs 0.247, essentially no gap) -- the same sequence #31 already flagged as anomalous. The visual grid (3 examples/sequence, real|synthetic|seg-mask|depth-with|depth-without) confirms by eye: synthetic frames show no person/hand silhouette where the real frames clearly do.

da3_absrel_real_vs_synthetic.note: scored against the with-skeleton GT depth (the confirmed-correct variant), static and dynamic pixels separately

part2_synthetic_hands_free.da3_read: In golden_seq100 and party_seq101, DA3-Small is WORSE on synthetic input on both static and dynamic pixels (+11%/+34% and +15%/+7% respectively) -- the synthetic domain gap (DA3 is real-world-pretrained) hurts more broadly than any hands-removal benefit helps, so this comparison does not cleanly isolate a hands effect the way #31's mean-fill did (which changed only the hand pixels, nothing else). meal_seq131 is flat (0.207->0.206, 0.150->0.148) -- again the outlier.
part2_synthetic_hands_free.31_conclusion_survival: #31's 'hands are just occlusion, not signal corruption' does not get a clean re-test here: the synthetic stream's own domain gap confounds static and dynamic pixels together rather than isolating the hand. It neither confirms nor refutes #31 -- it shows the synthetic substitution is the wrong tool for this specific question, unlike the mean-fill masking #31 used.

part2_meal_seq131_anomaly.read: Does NOT reproduce the anomaly under the standard #31 statistic (median of per-pair differences): synthetic vs vanilla is a wash (+0.197 deg, synthetic better on only 19/40 pairs) -- nothing like random_matched's clean ~4 deg edge. The group medians (7.017 vs 12.590) look like a big synthetic win, but that is driven by a handful of extreme pairs (several pairs where synthetic reads near-identity, ~0.13-0.16 deg, alongside others where it is far worse than vanilla, e.g. pair 27: 20.98 -> 40.55, pair 29: 66.92 -> 80.96) -- reporting only the group medians here would have been misleading, which is why both statistics are logged.

acceptance_summary.i_which_variants: both #28 and #31 used skeleton_flag=True consistently for seg and depth -- no mismatch to find
acceptance_summary.ii_does_with_skeleton_depth_contain_the_: yes -- confirmed on all three sequences, >=99.5% of dynamic pixels differ from the without-skeleton variant by >5cm, and the with-skeleton depth values are near-camera as expected for a hand/body
acceptance_summary.iv_is_synthetic_hands_free: yes by visual inspection (grid PNGs) and in 2/3 sequences by photometric diff; meal_seq131 does not show the same gap
acceptance_summary.v_does_31_conclusion_survive_synthetic_r: not testable cleanly this way -- synthetic's own domain gap confounds static/dynamic together; the meal_seq131 pose anomaly specifically does not reproduce under synthetic input (paired-difference stat is a wash)
